legend: Let rad(n)%%ZSMJ0%% denote the product of all distinct prime divisors of the number n%%ZSMJ1%%. For example, rad(504)%%ZSMJ2%% = rad(23⋅32⋅7)%%ZSMJ3%% =2⋅3⋅7%%ZSMJ4%% =42%%ZSMJ5%%. We define rad(1)=1%%ZSMJ6%%.

The statement of this problem is simple: you have an array a%%ZSMJ7%% of size n%%ZSMJ8%%. You are given q%%ZSMJ9%% queries [ℓ;r]%%ZSMJ10%%, and you need to compute rad of the product of the numbers aℓ,aℓ+1,…,ar%%ZSMJ11%%, that is: rad(r∏i=ℓai)=rad(aℓ×aℓ+1×⋯×ar)%%ZSMJ12%% Since this number can be quite large, output it modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ13%%.
input: The first line of input contains two numbers n,q%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤n,q≤5⋅105%%ZSMJ15%%), the number of elements in the array and the number of queries.
The second line of input contains n%%ZSMJ16%% numbers ai%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤ai≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ18%%), the array a%%ZSMJ19%%.
In the following q%%ZSMJ20%% lines, two numbers ℓ,r%%ZSMJ21%% (1≤ℓ≤r≤n%%ZSMJ22%%) are given, which are the boundaries of the next query.
output: In q%%ZSMJ23%% lines of output, print one number per line, the answer to the problem modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ24%%.
